advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make directive detection tolerant of HCL whitespace-trim markers (`~`) so `%{~ for ... ~}` pushes loop bindings and `%{ endfor ~}` pops the scope.
evidence: HCL template directives support trim markers: `%{~ for x in xs ~}` and `%{ endfor ~}` are valid and common in Terraform templates, and their interpolation body would be e.g. `~ for x in xs ~` / `endfor ~`, which neither the `^\s*for` anchor nor the exact `== "endfor"` check matches.
ABSENCE: no test covers a directive with a `~` trim marker; test_template_directives_are_not_reported_as_undeclared_roots uses only untrimmed `%{ for k, v in items }` / `%{ endfor }`.
advisory.finding: The `%{ endfor }` scope-pop and `%{ for ... }` scope-push use string matches that do not account for HCL whitespace-trim markers (`~`), e.g. `%{~ for k in xs }` / `%{ endfor ~}`. For a trimmed `for`, `_FOR_BINDINGS = re.compile(r'^\s*for\s+...')` does not match a body of `~ for k in xs`, so k is never pushed into scope and `${k}` is flagged as a FALSE POSITIVE; for a trimmed `endfor`, `expr.strip() == 'endfor'` is False, so the loop scope is never popped and every later undeclared reference is SILENTLY ACCEPTED (a fail-open guard miss).
advisory.suggested_fix: Normalize the expression before matching: strip leading/trailing `~` (e.g. `expr.strip().strip('~').strip()`) prior to the `_FOR_BINDINGS.match` and the `endfor` comparison.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Restrict declared_vars to top-level `key =` entries of the templatefile() map (depth 1), not identifiers at any brace depth.
evidence: The regex scans the ENTIRE brace span `text[open_brace:j]`, so a value like `cfg = { inner = merge(...) }` contributes both `cfg` and `inner` to the allowed set even though only `cfg` is an in-template variable.
advisory.finding: `declared_vars` treats any `identifier =` occurring anywhere inside the templatefile() variable-map braces as a declared variable, including keys nested in inner objects/maps passed as a value. Because BUILTIN_ROOTS plus these names form the `allowed` set, an interpolation whose root is not a top-level map key but coincidentally matches a nested `key =` name is accepted — the allow-list can silently over-permit, weakening the guard.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider reporting all undeclared roots in an interpolation instead of breaking on the first.
advisory.finding: In check_repo the per-interpolation loop `break`s after the first out-of-scope root, so an expression referencing two undeclared roots (e.g. `${A + B}`) reports only A. The build still fails, but the operator sees an incomplete list and must re-run after each fix.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that invokes the gate (main() or subprocess) over a tree with an unescaped interpolation and asserts a non-zero exit code.
evidence: tests/unit/test_check_templatefile_escapes.py:89: `assert proc.returncode == 0, proc.stderr` is the ONLY returncode assertion
search for `main(` in the test file returns no matches — main() is never invoked directly
scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py:254-273 main() maps `if not findings: return 0` else `return 1`; this branch to exit 1 is never exercised

Named violating input: running the gate over a tree containing an unescaped `${PARAMS}` (as in test_undeclared_reference_is_rejected) must exit 1, but no test asserts a non-zero exit / subprocess returncode==1
advisory.finding: No test asserts the gate exits NON-ZERO when a defect is present; only returncode==0 on the clean committed tree is checked. The guard's load-bearing contract ('makes the guard exit non-zero', per the commit message) — the main() count/exit-1 mapping — is untested, so main() could be refactored to always return 0 while every test stays green.
scenarios: A refactor of main() that drops or inverts the exit-code mapping ships green; the gate passes make lint even when it detects a defect
advisory.suggested_fix: Add: `proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(GATE), '--root', str(tmp_path)], ...)` over a tmp_path seeded with an undeclared `${PARAMS}` template, and `assert proc.returncode == 1`; optionally assert the count message is present in proc.stderr.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert Finding.render() contains the line/col/root and the `$${` guidance for a known defect.
evidence: scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py:89-103 Finding.render() builds the human-facing `path:line:col: unescaped '${' referencing undeclared 'root'` message
grep for `.render()` in the test file: only `Unresolved.render()` (line 225) is asserted; Finding.render() appears only inside an f-string in a negative assertion (line 252)
advisory.finding: Finding.render() output content is never asserted (only Unresolved.render is), so the stderr message format for a real escape finding — the line:col:root text a developer reads — is not regression-covered.
scenarios: The Finding message format is broken/renamed; tests stay green because only the .root/.line dataclass fields are asserted
